top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is the clearest game-changer on the slate: a simple principle, a small molecule forcing proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, shown in vitro, in cells and structurally, reproduced widely, and now a routine tool that reaches targets inhibitors could not. The three-name allocation fits the limit and one citation framed on E3 recruitment covers both the PROTAC and cereblon branches, though Ciulli is a real omission and clinical maturity is unverified. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles come second for proven impact but have unsettled attribution among six names; C-N coupling is third as a mature but less novel extension of the 2010 prize; no award is last because a sound candidate exists.
